newsitem.title: FRANCE: No delay to EMU allowed for - EU's de Silguy.
newsitem.headline: No delay to EMU allowed for - EU's de Silguy.

text.p: EU finance ministers will try this weekend to agree the date next year for selecting countries which qualify for monetary union, but any idea of delaying the EMU launch is not allowed for by the Maastricht treaty, European Monetary Affairs Commissioner Yves Thibault de Silguy said in a newspaper interview on Friday.
De Silguy told French daily La Tribune that the treaty only allowed for an advance of the January 1, 1999 start date.
He said that he did not see the issue of a delay being raised at the informal meeting of European Union ministers in the Dutch seaside town of Noordwijk.

Asked in the interview if he expected ministers to raise the subject of a delay to the start of EMU, de Silguy replied: "I do not expect so because a delay is not possible, short of changing the (Maastricht) treaty." The treaty is clear on this, he said.
He said the treaty did allow for a decision before the end of 1997 to change the date, but only to advance the launch and only if budgetary, economic and monetary conditions were fulfilled.
The finance ministers gather on Friday in Noordwijk but the main working session is on Saturday.
